distractorNotes: Reversed: the first model had the phosphates on the inside.
Reversed: the model had three chains, and the passage never says her data pointed to three.
Wrong timing: Pauling's model came in early 1953, after the Cambridge attempt of November 1951.
Outside the passage: no count of bases per turn figures in her objection.

answer.text: allowed for far less water than her measurements showed
answer.line: Paragraph 8 says the model allowed for only a fraction of the water her measurements showed, and it was abandoned.

steps: Find the first Cambridge model: paragraph 8, sentence 3, November 1951.
Read the next sentence for her objection. Her objection was water.
Use the model's own description as a filter. Three chains, phosphates inside: a choice that flips either one is out.

choices.text: put the phosphate groups on the outside of the helix
choices.note: The first model had the phosphates on the inside. Outside is where the 1953 model put the backbones, which is why it sounds familiar.

choices.text: contained two chains when her data pointed to three
choices.note: The model had three chains, not two, and nothing says her data pointed to three. The choice swaps the counts.

choices.text: copied the three-chain structure that Pauling had already published
choices.note: Pauling's three-chain model came in early 1953, so a model built in November 1951 could not copy it.

choices.text: allowed for far less water than her measurements showed
choices.note: Sentence 4: only a fraction of the water the fibers held.

choices.text: placed the bases ten to a turn instead of eleven
choices.note: Bases per turn never come up in her objection. This one needs outside knowledge.
